newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ross may face new Solomon mine claims.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ross may face new Solomon mine claims.

text.p: A law firm representing Solomon Island villagers seeking to negotiate a new compensation package over the proposed Gold Ridge mine project said it will consider further legal actions against Ross Mining NL if the project is granted a government mining lease.
"We will have to think about further legal actions if the mining lease goes through," Nick Styant-Brown, a lawyer with Slater and gordon legal firm told Reuters.
Styant-Brown said a constitutional challenge to a existing compensation plan proposed by Ross has been lodged in the Solomons in an effort to delay granting of the lease pending a new agreement.

Despite formal approval earlier this year from the Minister of Energy, Water and Mineral Resources on the impact of the project on the environment, Styant-Brown said the nearby Tetri River faced pollution caused by mine sediment.
Ross Mining has maintained its environmental system would enable it to contain sediment from the mine
"We are prepared to reopen additional environmental issues," Styant-Brown said.
But he denied the actions were designed to sidetrack the A$61.6 million project.
"We don't want to stop it... that's not our intention, Styant-Brown said.

He said the firm would seek from Ross Mining a more far-reaching compensation package than the one currently on the table that includes villagers from the nearby Guadacanal Plains district as well as in the immediate mine area.
The current proposal included payment of a 1.5 percent gross royalty from the mine, with 1.2 percent going to landowners and the rest to the local province.
Ross Mining also was spending about A$2 million to build a new village for locals dislocated by the mine.
Ross Mining executives had said they hoped to obtain the mining lease on March 12, but now acknowledge thed latest legal action could delay the approval.
The project's design called for production of around one million ounces of gold over 10 years at an average cash cost of under A$300 an ounce.
